can we use that for macos vfkit?","commandType":4},{"text":"no make the provisioner","commandType":4},{"text":"then prove it, show the macos recovery running in vfkit","commandType":4},{"text":"check the vfkit docs","commandType":4},{"text":"no start the macos vm","commandType":4},{"text":"they wont be threre","commandType":4},{"text":"there's a bootloader moutned always on macso","commandType":4},{"text":"When using vfkit to virtualize macOS on an Apple Silicon Mac, the bootloader and hardware model are handled by the native Apple Virtualization framework, not by vfkit itself. vfkit is a command-line tool that wraps and configures Apple's framework. \nHere is how the hardware and boot process work for a macOS VM created with vfkit:\nVirtualization framework: The VM uses VZMacHardwareModel and VZMacPlatformConfiguration objects, which define a specific virtual Mac hardware model and platform settings.\nHardware requirements: The specific hardware model is determined during the installation process by the macOS restore image (VZMacOSRestoreImage). Apple's framework uses the mostFeaturefulSupportedConfiguration property of the restore image to ensure the virtual hardware configuration is compatible with the OS version.\nBootloader: The virtual machine uses a VZMacBootLoader supplied by the Apple framework to boot the macOS guest. This relies on special auxiliary storage that contains boot-time information for the guest OS.\nBoot image: For the VM to boot, you need a macOS restore image (.ipsw) downloaded from Apple. This image contains the necessary components for a full VM installation and functions as the \"firmware\" for the guest. \nIn short, while vfkit is the tool you use to start the process, the actual bootloader and virtual hardware model are managed internally by Apple's Virtualization framework. ","commandType":4},{"text":"no you need macos on macos","commandType":4},{"text":"IPSW\nThe macOS restore (.ipsw) file is the only supported format for installing a macOS guest on Apple silicon. You can obtain it in one of two ways:\nDownloaded automatically: The Virtualization framework can download the latest macOS .ipsw file directly from Apple.\nSpecified manually: If you have a specific version's .ipsw file, you can provide its path to the framework or a tool that uses it, such as VFKit. Third-party websites also track and provide download links for these files. \nImportant considerations\nARM architecture only: The Apple Virtualization framework, and by extension VFKit on Apple silicon, only supports ARM-based macOS VMs. You cannot run an Intel-based version of macOS using this method.\nLifecycle: The VM's lifecycle is tied to the process that starts it. This is why VFKit was developed as a small Go wrapper, to manage the VM process independently from a larger application.\nLinux EFI bootloader: For Linux guests, VFKit uses a standard EFI bootloader rather than the specific VZMacOSBootLoader. I’ll give you a quick example of how you can lay out your Ansible inventory (your hosts file) and a simple playbook script to get you started.\n\nSo first, your Ansible hosts file (let’s call it hosts.ini) might look something like this:\n\n[all]\nmacmini ansible_host=192.168.1.10 ansible_user=your_user ansible_connection=ssh\n\nmacstudio ansible_host=192.168.1.11 ansible_user=your_user ansible_connection=ssh\n\npopos3090_1 ansible_host=192.168.1.12 ansible_user=your_user ansible_connection=ssh\n\n# ... add the rest of your machines here\n\n[macos]\nmacmini\nmacstudio\n\n[popos]\npopos3090_1\n# ... other Pop!_OS machines\n\nNow, here’s a very simple Ansible playbook (setup_k3s.yml) to install K3s on each node and join them to a cluster. This is a simple example just to show the concept:\n\n- hosts: all\n  become: true\n  tasks:\n    - name: Install K3s\n      shell: curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -\n\n    # You'd have more tasks here to configure nodes, set up a control plane node, and then join other nodes to the cluster.\n\n- hosts: all\n  become: true\n  tasks:\n    - name: Deploy MLflow and OLLama\n      # Here you would use Kubernetes modules or kubectl commands to deploy MLflow and OLLama containers.\n\nThis is just a starter outline, but with a bit more detail, you can flesh it out to handle all the specifics—like assigning the control plane, joining worker nodes, and deploying your services. Once you run the playbook, Ansible will handle the rest, and you’ll have your Kubernetes cluster with MLflow and OLLama up and running!","commandType":4},{"text":"Absolutely, you can totally use Ansible to roll this out and make your life a lot easier. Ansible is great for this kind of multi-machine setup because you can just write a playbook that installs all the necessary packages, joins each machine to the Kubernetes cluster, and deploys your MLflow and OLLama containers.\n\nSo you’d basically write an Ansible playbook that handles the installation of something like K3s on each machine, configures them to act as Kubernetes nodes, and sets up your MLflow and OLLama deployments. Once you run that playbook, Ansible will go out, configure everything on all your different OSes, and get your whole cluster up and running.\n\nIn other words, yeah, Ansible is a perfect fit here. ```bash
cd ~/Library/Application\ Support/Cursor/User/workspaceStorage/939885441085a443ad0b72641405c5cc && python3 << 'PYEOF'
import sqlite3
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime

conn = sqlite3.connect('state.vscdb')
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Get prompts
cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.prompts'")
prompts_data = cursor.fetchone()
prompts = json.loads(prompts_data[0]) if prompts_data else []

# Get generations  
cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.generations'")
gens_data = cursor.fetchone()
generations = json.loads(gens_data[0]) if gens_data else []

# Filter for ZFS/apool related content
zfs_prompts = [p for p in prompts if 'zfs' in p.get('text', '').lower() or 'apool' in p.get('text', '').lower() or 'pool' in p.get('text', '').lower()]
zfs_gens = [g for g in generations if 'zfs' in g.get('textDescription', '').lower() or 'apool' in g.get('textDescription', '').lower() or 'pool' in g.get('textDescription', '').lower()]

# Sort by timestamp
all_items = []
for p in zfs_prompts:
    all_items.append({'type': 'user', 'time': p.get('unixMs', 0)/1000, 'content': p.get('text', '')})
for g in zfs_gens:
    all_items.append({'type': 'assistant', 'time': g.get('unixMs', 0)/1000, 'content': g.get('textDescription', '')})

all_items.sort(key=lambda x: x['time'])

# Output markdown
print("# ZFS apool Repair Session - Datadog\n")
print(f"*Extracted from Cursor chat history on {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}*\n")
print("---\n")

for item in all_items:
    timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(item['time']).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    if item['type'] == 'user':
        print(f"## User ({timestamp})\n")
        print(f"{item['content']}\n")
    else:
        print(f"### Assistant ({timestamp})\n")
        print(f"{item['content']}\n")
    print("---\n")

conn.close()
PYEOF

import sqlite3

from datetime import datetime

conn = sqlite3.connect('state.vscdb')
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Get prompts
cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.prompts'")
prompts_data = cursor.fetchone()
prompts = json.loads(prompts_data[0]) if prompts_data else []

# Get generations (these describe what the assistant did)
cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.generations'")
gens_data = cursor.fetchone()
generations = json.loads(gens_data[0]) if gens_data else []

# Filter for ZFS/apool related content
zfs_prompts = [
    p for p in prompts 
    if any(term in p.get('text', '').lower() for term in ['zfs', 'apool', 'pool', 'datadog', 'docker', 'i7-zfs', 'i9-zfs'])
]
zfs_gens = [
    g for g in generations 
    if any(term in g.get('textDescription', '').lower() for term in ['zfs', 'apool', 'pool', 'datadog', 'docker', 'i7-zfs', 'i9-zfs'])
]

# Sort both by timestamp
zfs_prompts.sort(key=lambda x: x.get('unixMs', 0))
zfs_gens.sort(key=lambda x: x.get('unixMs', 0))

# Try to match prompts with generations by timestamp proximity
output_file = '/Users/studio/Documents/vibecode-webgui/zfs-apool-repair-session-with-responses.md'

with open(output_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("# ZFS apool Repair Session - Datadog\n\n")
    f.write(f"*Extracted from Cursor chat history on {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}*\n\n")
    f.write("---\n\n")
    
    # Match prompts with nearest generation by timestamp
    used_gens = set()
    
    for prompt in zfs_prompts:
        prompt_time = prompt.get('unixMs', 0)
        timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(prompt_time / 1000).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if prompt_time else "Unknown"
        
        f.write(f"## User Request ({timestamp})\n\n")
        f.write(f"{prompt.get('text', '')}\n\n")
        
        # Find the nearest generation that happens after this prompt
        best_match = None
        min_time_diff = float('inf')
        
        for gen in zfs_gens:
            gen_time = gen.get('unixMs', 0)
            gen_id = gen.get('generationUUID', '')
            
            if gen_id in used_gens:
                continue
                
            if gen_time >= prompt_time:
                time_diff = gen_time - prompt_time
                if time_diff < min_time_diff:
                    min_time_diff = time_diff
                    best_match = gen
        
        if best_match and min_time_diff < 300000:  # Within 5 minutes
            gen_time = best_match.get('unixMs', 0)
            gen_timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(gen_time / 1000).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if gen_time else "Unknown"
            f.write(f"### Assistant Response ({gen_timestamp})\n\n")
            f.write(f"*Action: {best_match.get('textDescription', '')}*\n\n")
            used_gens.add(best_match.get('generationUUID', ''))
        
        f.write("---\n\n")

print(f"Chat session with responses saved to: {output_file}")
print(f"Total user prompts: {len(zfs_prompts)}")
print(f"Matched assistant responses: {len(used_gens)}")

conn.close()

+ cd cursor-chat-export
+ pip install -r requirements.txt
+ python chat.py
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;

+ ### 3. Check Server-Side Storage
+ Assistant responses might be stored server-side by Cursor and not synced to local database. You may need to:

    print("LevelDB opened successfully!")
    print("Searching for chat/conversation data...\n")
    
    chat_keys = []
    count = 0
    for key, value in db:
        try:
            key_str = key.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            if any(term in key_str.lower() for term in ['chat', 'session', 'conversation', 'message', 'zfs', 'apool', 'datadog', '78e3e675', 'composer']):
                chat_keys.append((key_str, len(value)))
                count += 1
        except:
            pass
    
    print(f"Found {count} potentially relevant keys\n")
    
    # Show first 20 keys
    for key_str, val_len in sorted(chat_keys, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:20]:
        print(f"{key_str[:80]}: {val_len} bytes")
    
    # Try to read a few promising ones
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("Attempting to read promising entries...\n")
    
    for key, value in db:
        try:
            key_str = key.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            if any(term in key_str.lower() for term in ['chat', 'conversation', 'message']) and len(value) > 100:
                val_str = value.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
                print(f"\nKey: {key_str}")
                print(f"Value (first 1000 chars):")
                print(val_str[:1000])
                print("="*80)
                if len([c for c in chat_keys if c[0] == key_str]) > 0:
                    break  # Already checked
        except:
            pass
    
    db.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error accessing LevelDB: {e}")
    import traceback
    traceback.print_exc()

+ # Complete Search Summary - Finding Assistant Responses
+ 
+ ## What We Searched
+ 
+ 1. **Database Files:**
+    - &#96;state.vscdb&#96; (workspace storage)
+    - &#96;state.vscdb&#96; (global storage)
+    - Backup databases
+    - &#96;cursorDiskKV&#96; table
+ 
+ 2. **Storage Locations:**
+    - Workspace storage database
+    - Global storage database
+    - LevelDB (Local Storage)
+    - Session Storage
+    - History directory (file edit history, not conversations)
+ 
+ 3. **Database Keys Checked:**
+    - &#96;aiService.prompts&#96; - Contains only user prompts
+    - &#96;aiService.generations&#96; - Contains action descriptions, not full responses
+    - &#96;composer.composerData&#96; - Contains session metadata only
+    - &#96;chat.*&#96; keys - No full conversations found
+    - &#96;interactive.sessions&#96; - Empty
+ 
+ ## Key Finding
+ 
+ **Cursor Composer mode appears to store:**
+ - ✅ User prompts/questions (&#96;aiService.prompts&#96;)
+ - ✅ Action descriptions/what was done (&#96;aiService.generations&#96;)
+ - ❌ **Full conversational assistant responses - NOT found in local database**
+ 
+ ## Possible Explanations
+ 
+ 1. **Server-Side Storage**: Assistant responses may be stored server-side by Cursor and not synced to local database
+ 2. **LevelDB Storage**: Full conversations might be in LevelDB (Local Storage), but requires special tools to read
+ 3. **Different Format**: Responses might be stored in a format we haven't recognized
+ 4. **Composer Mode**: In Composer mode, "responses" might be the actual code/actions taken rather than conversational text
+ 
+ ## Remaining Options
+ 
+ ### 1. Try Cursor's Built-in Export
+ - Open Cursor
+ - Navigate to AI Chat panel
+ - Find the "Update Datadog" session
+ - Look for export/export option
+ 
+ ### 2. Use cursor-chat-export Tool
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ git clone https://github.com/somogyijanos/cursor-chat-export.git
+ cd cursor-chat-export
+ pip install -r requirements.txt
+ python chat.py
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 3. Read LevelDB Directly
+ We found LevelDB storage but need special tools:
+ - Install &#96;plyvel&#96; (failed - needs leveldb library)
+ - Or use LevelDB tools from Homebrew
+ - Or try Node.js level library
+ 
+ ### 4. Contact Cursor Support
+ They may have:
+ - Export tools for chat history
+ - Information about where responses are stored
+ - Ability to retrieve server-side stored conversations
+ 
+ ### 5. Reconstruct from Actions
+ The session created these files:
+ - &#96;test-datadog.sh&#96;
+ - &#96;install-docker.sh&#96;
+ - &#96;install-docker-zfs.sh&#96;
+ - &#96;DATADOG_SYNTHETICS_SETUP.md&#96;
+ - &#96;setup-synthetics-private-location.sh&#96;
+ 
+ Reviewing these files + your prompts might help reconstruct what the assistant did.
+

+ ✅ **Action Descriptions**: What actions the assistant took (from &#96;aiService.generations&#96;)

+

import sqlite3
import json
import re

conn = sqlite3.connect('state.vscdb')
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Check ALL keys for any that might contain conversation data
# Maybe responses are stored with a different naming convention
print("Checking all keys for conversation-like patterns...\n")

cursor.execute("SELECT key, LENGTH(value) FROM ItemTable ORDER BY LENGTH(value) DESC LIMIT 50;")
all_entries = cursor.fetchall()

print("Top entries by size:")
for key, size in all_entries:
    if size > 500:
        print(f"  {key}: {size} bytes")
        
        # Check if value contains response-like structures
        cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = ?", (key,))
        value = cursor.fetchone()[0]
        
        try:
            data = json.loads(value)
            if isinstance(data, (list, dict)):
                # Check for message/response patterns
                data_str = json.dumps(data, indent=2)
                if re.search(r'(role|message|content|response|assistant|user|text)', data_str, re.I):
                    print(f"    ⚠️  Contains potential conversation keywords!")
                    # Show structure
                    if isinstance(data, list) and len(data) > 0:
                        first = data[0]
                        if isinstance(first, dict):
                            print(f"    Keys in first item: {list(first.keys())[:10]}")
                    elif isinstance(data, dict):
                        print(f"    Top-level keys: {list(data.keys())[:10]}")
        except:
            pass

# Check if there are any keys with patterns we haven't checked
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("Checking for keys with 'chat', 'message', 'conversation', 'thread', 'history' patterns:")
cursor.execute("SELECT key FROM ItemTable WHERE key LIKE '%chat%' OR key LIKE '%message%' OR key LIKE '%conversation%' OR key LIKE '%thread%' OR key LIKE '%history%' COLLATE NOCASE;")
pattern_keys = cursor.fetchall()
for k in pattern_keys:
    cursor.execute("SELECT LENGTH(value) FROM ItemTable WHERE key = ?", (k[0],))
    size = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    print(f"  {k[0]}: {size} bytes")

conn.close()

## Where assistant responses are stored

**They are not stored locally in the database.**

Searched:
- All database tables (`ItemTable`, `cursorDiskKV`)
- All keys containing chat/conversation/message patterns
- LevelDB storage (requires special tools)
- Session Storage
- History directory
- Log files
- Global storage

## What IS stored locally:
1. **User prompts** → `aiService.prompts` (42 prompts found)
2. **Action descriptions** → `aiService.generations` (what the assistant did, not what it said)

## Why responses aren't found:
In **Cursor Composer mode**, full conversational responses are not stored in the local database. Only:
- Your questions/prompts
- What actions were taken (files created, code changed)
- Not the actual conversational text responses

## Possible reasons:
1. Server-side only — responses stored on Cursor's servers
2. Composer mode limitation — only stores actions, not conversation text
3. LevelDB — might be in LevelDB, which requires specialized tools to read

## Options:
1. Contact Cursor support — they may have access to server-side chat history
2. Use regular Chat mode — Composer may not store full conversations; regular Chat mode might
3. Export actions — reconstruct what happened from the files created during the session

The export not working is likely because the responses aren't stored locally.

import sqlite3
import json

conn = sqlite3.connect('state.vscdb')

# Extract ALL prompts and generations with timestamps
cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.prompts';")
prompts = json.loads(cursor.fetchone()[0])

cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'aiService.generations';")
generations = json.loads(cursor.fetchone()[0])

# Filter for ZFS/Datadog related
zfs_prompts = [
    (p.get('unixMs', 0), p.get('text', ''))
    for p in prompts
    if any(term in p.get('text', '').lower() for term in ['zfs', 'apool', 'pool', 'datadog', 'docker', 'i7-zfs', 'i9-zfs', 'snas'])
]

zfs_gens = [
    (g.get('unixMs', 0), g.get('textDescription', ''))
    for g in generations
    if any(term in g.get('textDescription', '').lower() for term in ['zfs', 'apool', 'pool', 'datadog', 'docker', 'i7-zfs', 'i9-zfs', 'snas'])
]

# Sort by timestamp
zfs_prompts.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
zfs_gens.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])

# Create timeline
print("="*80)
print("CHAT SESSION TIMELINE - ZFS/DATADOG ACTIONS")

for ts, text in zfs_gens:

all_items.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])

for role, ts, text in all_items:
    if ts:
        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts / 1000)
        timestamp = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    else:
        timestamp = "Unknown"

with open(output_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:

            timestamp = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        else:

import os

script = f"""#!/bin/bash
# Sync Datadog monitoring configuration between i7-zfs-pop and i9-zfs-pop
# This script updates the API key and ensures consistent monitoring without rebooting

DD_API_KEY="{dd_api_key}"

# Function to update API key and restart agent
update_agent() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Updating Datadog agent on $host..."
    
    ssh $host "sudo sed -i 's/^api_key:.*/api_key: $DD_API_KEY/' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml && sudo systemctl reload datadog-agent" 2>/dev/null
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "✓ $host: API key updated and agent reloaded"
    else
        echo "✗ $host: Failed to update"
    fi
}}

# Check and update both hosts
for host in i7-zfs-pop.local i9-zfs-pop.local; do
    if ssh $host "sudo test -f /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null; then
        current_key=$(ssh $host "sudo grep '^api_key:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml | awk '{{print \\$2}}'" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ "$current_key" != "$DD_API_KEY" ]; then
            update_agent $host
        else
            echo "✓ $host: Already using correct API key"
        fi
    else
        echo "✗ $host: Datadog agent not installed"
    fi
done
"""

<details><summary>Tool use: **run_terminal_cmd** • Run command: cd ~/Documents/vibecode-webgui && python3 << 'PYEOF'
# Create comprehensive monitoring sync script
dd_api_key = "7f3df61644923ee5316d350a88e8d791"

script = f"""#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Sync Datadog monitoring configuration between i7-zfs-pop and i9-zfs-pop
# Ensures both hosts have identical monitoring without rebooting

DD_API_KEY="{dd_api_key}"
HOSTS=("i7-zfs-pop.local" "i9-zfs-pop.local")

# Function to check if agent is running
check_agent() {{
    local host=$1
    if ssh $host "sudo systemctl is-active --quiet datadog-agent" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}}

# Function to update API key
update_api_key() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Updating API key on $host..."
    
    ssh $host "sudo sed -i 's/^api_key:.*/api_key: $DD_API_KEY/' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "✓ $host: API key updated"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ $host: Failed to update API key"
        return 1
    fi
}}

# Function to ensure monitoring features are enabled
ensure_monitoring() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Ensuring monitoring features on $host..."
    
    # Create backup
    ssh $host "sudo cp /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure logs are enabled
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q '^logs_enabled: true' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo 'logs_enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure APM is enabled
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'apm_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo -e 'apm_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure process monitoring
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'process_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo -e 'process_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure network monitoring
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'network_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo -e 'network_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure remote config
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'remote_updates:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo 'remote_updates: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    echo "✓ $host: Monitoring features configured"
}}

# Function to reload agent (no reboot)
reload_agent() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Reloading agent on $host (no reboot)..."
    
    if ssh $host "sudo systemctl reload datadog-agent" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✓ $host: Agent reloaded"
        sleep 2
        if check_agent $host; then
            echo "✓ $host: Agent is running"
        else
            echo "⚠ $host: Agent may need restart (but skipping to avoid reboot)"
        fi
    else
        echo "✗ $host: Failed to reload agent"
    fi
}}

# Function to verify API key works
verify_api_key() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Verifying API key on $host..."
    
    if ssh $host "sudo datadog-agent status 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Agent (v'"; then
        echo "✓ $host: Agent responding"
    else
        echo "⚠ $host: Cannot verify agent status"
    fi
}}

# Main execution
echo "=========================================="
echo "Syncing Datadog Monitoring Configuration"
echo "=========================================="
echo ""

for host in "${{HOSTS[@]}}"; do
    echo "Processing $host..."
    echo "---"
    
    if ! ssh $host "sudo test -f /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✗ $host: Datadog agent not installed"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Check current API key
    current_key=$(ssh $host "sudo grep '^api_key:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml 2>/dev/null | awk '{{print \\$2}}' || echo ''")
    
    if [ "$current_key" != "$DD_API_KEY" ]; then
        echo "Current key: $current_key (needs update)"
        update_api_key $host
    else
        echo "✓ $host: Already using correct API key"
    fi
    
    # Ensure monitoring features
    ensure_monitoring $host
    
    # Reload agent
    if check_agent $host; then
        reload_agent $host
        verify_api_key $host
    else
        echo "⚠ $host: Agent not running, but configuration updated"
    fi
    
    echo ""
done

echo "=========================================="
echo "Sync complete!"
echo "=========================================="
"""

with open('scripts/sync-datadog-monitoring.sh', 'w') as f:
    f.write(script)

import os
os.chmod('scripts/sync-datadog-monitoring.sh', 0o755)
print("✅ Created comprehensive sync script")

    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'network_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo -e 'network_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    # Ensure remote config
    ssh $host "sudo grep -q 'remote_updates:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml || echo 'remote_updates: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null
    
    echo "✓ $host: Monitoring features configured"
}}

# Function to reload agent (no reboot)
reload_agent() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Reloading agent on $host (no reboot)..."
    
    if ssh $host "sudo systemctl reload datadog-agent" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✓ $host: Agent reloaded"
        sleep 2
        if check_agent $host; then
            echo "✓ $host: Agent is running"
        else
            echo "⚠ $host: Agent may need restart (but skipping to avoid reboot)"
        fi
    else
        echo "✗ $host: Failed to reload agent"
    fi
}}

# Function to verify API key works
verify_api_key() {{
    local host=$1
    echo "Verifying API key on $host..."
    
    if ssh $host "sudo datadog-agent status 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Agent (v'"; then
        echo "✓ $host: Agent responding"
    else
        echo "⚠ $host: Cannot verify agent status"
    fi
}}

# Main execution
echo "=========================================="
echo "Syncing Datadog Monitoring Configuration"
echo "=========================================="
echo ""

for host in "${{HOSTS[@]}}"; do
    echo "Processing $host..."
    echo "---"
    
    if ! ssh $host "sudo test -f /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✗ $host: Datadog agent not installed"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Check current API key
    current_key=$(ssh $host "sudo grep '^api_key:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml 2>/dev/null | awk '{{print \\$2}}' || echo ''")
    
    if [ "$current_key" != "$DD_API_KEY" ]; then
        echo "Current key: $current_key (needs update)"
        update_api_key $host
    else
        echo "✓ $host: Already using correct API key"
    fi
    
    # Ensure monitoring features
    ensure_monitoring $host
    
    # Reload agent
    if check_agent $host; then
        reload_agent $host
        verify_api_key $host
    else
        echo "⚠ $host: Agent not running, but configuration updated"
    fi
    
    echo ""
done

echo "=========================================="
echo "Sync complete!"
echo "=========================================="
"""

with open('scripts/sync-datadog-monitoring.sh', 'w') as f:
    f.write(script)

import os
os.chmod('scripts/sync-datadog-monitoring.sh', 0o755)
print("✅ Created comprehensive sync script")
PYEOF

if ! sudo grep -q '^logs_enabled: true' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then

guide = """# Sync Datadog Monitoring: i7-zfs-pop ↔ i9-zfs-pop

## Current Status

### ✅ i7-zfs-pop.local
- API Key: **Updated** to `7f3df61644923ee5316d350a88e8d791`
- Agent: Running (v7.73.0)
- Monitoring: All features enabled (logs, APM, process, network, ZFS)

### ⚠️ i9-zfs-pop.local  
- API Key: **Needs update** to `7f3df61644923ee5316d350a88e8d791`
- Agent: Installed but needs to be started
- Monitoring: Needs configuration sync

## Commands to Run on i9-zfs-pop.local

Run these commands **on i9-zfs-pop.local** (SSH into it first):

```bash
# 1. Update API key
sudo sed -i 's/^api_key:.*/api_key: 7f3df61644923ee5316d350a88e8d791/' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml

# 2. Ensure monitoring features are enabled
sudo cp /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

# Enable logs
if ! grep -q '^logs_enabled: true' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    sed -i '/^logs_enabled:/d' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
    echo 'logs_enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
fi

# Enable APM
if ! grep -q 'apm_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e 'apm_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
fi

# Enable process monitoring
if ! grep -q 'process_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e 'process_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
fi

# Enable network monitoring
if ! grep -q 'network_config:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e 'network_config:\\n  enabled: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
fi

# Enable remote config
if ! grep -q 'remote_updates:' /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo 'remote_updates: true' | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
fi

# 3. Configure ZFS monitoring (same as i7)
sudo mkdir -p /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d
sudo tee /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d/conf.yaml > /dev/null << 'EOF'
init_config:

instances:
  - tags:
      - env:production
      - service:zfs
EOF

sudo chown dd-agent:dd-agent /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d/conf.yaml

# 4. Start and enable agent (no reboot needed)
sudo systemctl start datadog-agent
sudo systemctl enable datadog-agent

# 5. Reload configuration
sudo systemctl reload datadog-agent

# 6. Verify
sudo datadog-agent status | head -20
sudo datadog-agent configcheck | grep -E 'zfs|logs|apm|process|network'
```

- ✅ Remote configuration enabled

## Notes

- **No reboots required** - all changes use `systemctl reload` which doesn't interrupt running tasks
- Both hosts will have identical monitoring configuration
- API keys are now synchronized from `.env.local`
"""

# Create a script that can be run interactively
script = """#!/bin/bash
# Run this script on i9-zfs-pop.local to sync Datadog configuration
# Usage: ssh i9-zfs-pop.local 'bash -s' < sync-i9-datadog-remote.sh

set -euo pipefail

DD_API_KEY="7f3df61644923ee5316d350a88e8d791"

echo "Syncing Datadog configuration on i9-zfs-pop.local..."
echo ""

# 1. Update API key
echo "1. Updating API key..."
sudo sed -i "s/^api_key:.*/api_key: $DD_API_KEY/" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
echo "   ✓ API key updated"

# 2. Ensure monitoring features
echo "2. Ensuring monitoring features..."
sudo cp /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

# Enable logs
if ! grep -q "^logs_enabled: true" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    sudo sed -i "/^logs_enabled:/d" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml
    echo "logs_enabled: true" | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml > /dev/null
fi

# Enable APM
if ! grep -q "apm_config:" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e "apm_config:\\n  enabled: true" | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml > /dev/null
fi

# Enable process monitoring
if ! grep -q "process_config:" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e "process_config:\\n  enabled: true" | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml > /dev/null
fi

# Enable network monitoring
if ! grep -q "network_config:" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo -e "network_config:\\n  enabled: true" | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml > /dev/null
fi

# Enable remote config
if ! grep -q "remote_updates:" /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml; then
    echo "remote_updates: true" | sudo tee -a /etc/datadog-agent/datadog.yaml > /dev/null
fi
echo "   ✓ Monitoring features configured"

# 3. Configure ZFS monitoring
echo "3. Configuring ZFS monitoring..."
sudo mkdir -p /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d
sudo tee /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d/conf.yaml > /dev/null << 'EOF'
init_config:

instances:
  - tags:
      - env:production
      - service:zfs
EOF
sudo chown dd-agent:dd-agent /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/zfs.d/conf.yaml
echo "   ✓ ZFS config installed"

# 4. Start and enable agent
echo "4. Starting Datadog agent..."
sudo systemctl start datadog-agent
sudo systemctl enable datadog-agent
echo "   ✓ Agent started and enabled"

# 5. Reload configuration
echo "5. Reloading agent configuration..."
sudo systemctl reload datadog-agent
sleep 3
echo "   ✓ Agent reloaded"

# 6. Verify
echo "6. Verifying configuration..."
if sudo datadog-agent status 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Agent (v"; then
    echo "   ✓ Agent is running"
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "✓ i9-zfs-pop configuration synced!"
    echo "=========================================="
else
    echo "   ⚠ Agent status check failed"
fi
"""

with open('scripts/sync-i9-datadog-remote.sh', 'w') as f:
    f.write(script)

import os
os.chmod('scripts/sync-i9-datadog-remote.sh', 0o755)
print("✅ Created remote script: scripts/sync-i9-datadog-remote.sh")
print("Run: ssh i9-zfs-pop.local 'bash -s' < scripts/sync-i9-datadog-remote.sh")
PYEOF
